gate: component paper: body-conducted non-audible murmur recognizer (skin-contact stethoscopic microphone, normal-speech HMM retrained with NAM, 20K-word dictation)
prep: no prep/ directory; plan and audits built by the writer; published topic table M12/body-conducted-sensor-noise-test-protocol reused append-only; checked notes for Jou 2004, Graciarena 2004 and Whisphone 2025 reused from the nasovoce work dir with quotes re-verified
time_frame: First public 2004-09: the IEICE Trans. Inf. & Syst. E89-D(1) 2006 paper is the English version (2004 IEICE Excellent Paper Award special section) of IEICE Trans. D-II J87-D-II(9), Sept. 2004, whose Table 1 is identical; both merged with the target (ieice2004-nakajima-nam-recognition, ieice-e89d-nakajima-nam-2006). Prior = first public before 2004-03; [concurrent] = 2004-03 to 2005-03. The group's ICASSP 2003 (2003-04) and Eurospeech 2003 (2003-09) papers report one earlier experiment with the same design and the same environment A-C rows; they are a distinct earlier publication (smaller described training set, three environments) and count once as a same-group prior. Heracleous et al. ASRU 2003 (iterative MLLR) is a separate same-group prior.
setting: One setting across slots: recognizers of speech that is not voiced speech picked up by an air microphone, i.e. speech produced without vocal-fold vibration (whisper, murmur, mimed or silently articulated speech) from any signal, and speech picked up by skin-, bone- or tissue-conducted sensors in any speaking mode. NAM is a body-conducted acoustic signal, so acoustic whisper recognition (air microphone), throat-microphone and bone-conduction recognition are inside the comparison population; non-acoustic silent-speech recognizers (EMG, ultrasound, video) are inside for the speaking-mode comparison (M04) and for novelty, but not for sensor-site or adaptation counts, where their design is not comparable.

inherited.M01: One male speaker reads ATR and JNAS sentences in NAM in a quiet room (group's 2003 protocol)
inherited.M02: Sentence transcripts without segmentation times (embedded re-estimation)
inherited.M06: Monophone 5-state 16-mixture HMMs, 12 MFCC + 12 delta + delta log power, Julius (Japanese Dictation Toolkit 1999)
inherited.M07: Toolkit 20K-word vocabulary and trigram language model, unchanged
inherited.M09: Offline study; visual checking only proposed

topics.inclusion_rule: Speech recognizers (text output) whose test input is a skin-, bone- or tissue-conducted acoustic sensor on the talker (throat or contact microphone, bone-conduction microphone, NAM or stethoscopic microphone, accelerometer), in any speaking mode; design compared is the body site of the sensor. Boundary: enhancement or conversion without a recognizer, speaker recognition and reviews are excluded; air-microphone whisper recognizers belong to the M04 topic; multiple reports of one experiment count once; the 2004 Japanese and 2006 English versions of the target are merged.
topics.pattern: ledger: body-conducted sensor term AND recognition term
topics.metric: word accuracy on large-vocabulary dictation, speaker dependence and noise condition matched

topics.inclusion_rule: Recognizers that decode text from speech produced without vocal-fold vibration (whisper, non-audible murmur, mimed or silently articulated speech), from any signal (air or body-conducted microphone, EMG, ultrasound, video, articulography); design compared is the speaking mode and the scale of the recognition task (isolated units versus large-vocabulary continuous dictation). Boundary: imagined or inner speech, voiced-speech recognizers that only mention whisper, whisper-versus-normal classifiers, conversion without a recognizer and reviews are excluded; multiple reports of one experiment count once.
topics.pattern: ledger: unvoiced speaking-mode term AND recognition term
topics.metric: word accuracy or recognition rate, vocabulary and speaker dependence matched

topics.inclusion_rule: Recognizers for whispered, murmured or body-conducted speech that obtain the acoustic model from normal (air-microphone, voiced) speech models by retraining, MAP or MLLR-family adaptation or speaker adaptive training, or that train on the target speaking mode from scratch; design compared is the transfer method and the amount of target-mode data. Boundary: conversion systems without a recognizer, enhancement front ends that leave the model unchanged, and reviews are excluded; multiple reports of one experiment count once.
topics.pattern: ledger: unvoiced or body-conducted term AND adaptation term AND recognition term
topics.metric: word accuracy versus amount of target-mode data

topics.inclusion_rule: Reused published table (same population as M05 body-conducted-sensor-with-air-microphone; design compared is whether noise tests expose the conducted sensor to the noise physically or add it digitally). Added for this review: dated counts at 2004-09 and whether the noise level and an air-microphone baseline in the same noise are reported.
topics.metric: word accuracy or WER under stated noise level
